description: Step 6 look-at-pronoun: inserts the missing 'at' in 'look + pronoun-object' surfaces (look me -> look at me). This fixture focuses on QUESTION-FORM PROTECTION — the rule fires on declarative/imperative surfaces but must NOT fire on questions or already-correct 'look at ...' phrasings. Expectations encode the VERIFIED behaviour of correctWithTutorRules() on current main. Complements the bundled look-at-pronoun.json with a protection-focused negative set.
fp_risk_note: 'look' is high-risk: it can be a linking verb or part of many (possibly separated) phrasal verbs, and question forms already place the particle correctly. The negative cases lock the protection behaviour: (1) modal yes/no questions already correct ('Can you look at me?'); (2) wh-questions ending in a stranded particle ('What are you looking at?'); (3) auxiliary questions already correct ('Do you look at them?'). None may trigger an 'at' insertion. The positives confirm the rule still fires on plain declarative/imperative 'look + pronoun'.

positive.notes: Declarative 'I look you' -> 'I look at you'.
'look him' -> 'look at him' (the rule inserts 'at'; it does not also fix 3rd-person agreement).

negative.notes: Question protection: modal yes/no question already correct; rule must not fire.
Question protection: wh-question with stranded particle; must not be touched.
Question protection: auxiliary question already correct; rule must abstain.
